questions.stem: A fast passenger train exactly 120 meters long is running at a uniform speed of 90 km/hr. How much exact time will it take to completely cross a stationary signal pole?
questions.explanation: First, convert speed from km/hr to m/s: 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. The distance to cross a pole is the length of the train itself (120m). Time = Distance / Speed = 120 / 25 = 4.8 seconds.

questions.stem: A heavy cargo train exactly 150 meters long is running at a speed of 72 km/hr. How much time will it firmly take to cross a stationary platform that is exactly 250 meters long?
questions.explanation: Convert speed to m/s: 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Total distance to cover = Length of train + Length of platform = 150 + 250 = 400 meters. Time = Distance / Speed = 400 / 20 = 20 seconds.

questions.stem: Two distinct trains, 140m and 160m long, seamlessly run at speeds of 60 km/hr and 40 km/hr respectively in opposite directions on parallel tracks. What is the exact time they take to completely cross each other?
questions.explanation: Since they run in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their speeds: 60 + 40 = 100 km/hr. In m/s: 100 * (5/18) = 250/9 m/s. Total distance to cover = sum of their lengths = 140 + 160 = 300m. Time = 300 / (250/9) = (300 * 9) / 250 = 2700 / 250 = 10.8 seconds.

questions.stem: A speeding train running at exactly 54 km/hr crosses a man running at exactly 9 km/hr in the exact same direction in exactly 12 seconds. What is the total length of the train?
questions.explanation: Since the man and train move in the same direction, relative speed = 54 - 9 = 45 km/hr. In m/s: 45 * (5/18) = 12.5 m/s. The distance covered to cross the man is the length of the train itself. Length = Relative Speed * Time = 12.5 m/s * 12 seconds = 150 meters.

questions.stem: A train fully passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing safely on the platform in 20 seconds. If the speed of the train is exactly 54 km/hr, what is the exact length of the platform?
questions.explanation: Speed = 54 km/hr = 15 m/s. The train crosses the man (a point object) in 20 seconds. So, Train Length = 15 * 20 = 300m. It crosses the platform in 36 seconds. Total distance = Train Length + Platform Length (P). So, (300 + P) = 15 * 36 = 540. P = 540 - 300 = 240 meters.

questions.stem: Two individual trains are running precisely in the same direction at 65 km/hr and 45 km/hr. The significantly faster train crosses a man sitting in the slower train in exactly 18 seconds. What is the exact length of the faster train?
questions.explanation: Since they move in the same direction, relative speed = 65 - 45 = 20 km/hr = 20 * (5/18) = 50/9 m/s. Since the faster train crosses a 'man' (a point) sitting in the slower train, the distance covered is only the length of the faster train. Length = Speed * Time = (50/9) * 18 = 100 meters.

questions.stem: A moving train travelling at 48 km/hr fully crosses another train, having exactly half its length and travelling in the opposite direction at 42 km/hr, in exactly 12 seconds. It also safely passes a railway platform in 45 seconds. The total length of the railway platform is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 48 + 42 = 90 km/hr = 25 m/s. Let the lengths of the trains be L and L/2. Total distance = 3L/2. 3L/2 = 25 m/s * 12s = 300m. So, 3L = 600m, and L = 200m. The first train's speed = 48 km/hr = 48 * (5/18) = 40/3 m/s. Let platform length be P. (200 + P) / (40/3) = 45. (200 + P) = 45 * 40 / 3 = 15 * 40 = 600m. P = 600 - 200 = 400 meters.
